{{short description|Elliptic functions}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''half-period ratio''' &tau; of an [[elliptic function]] is the ratio

:<math>\tau = \frac{\omega_2}{\omega_1}</math>

of the two [[fundamental pair of periods|half-periods]] <math>\frac{\omega_1}{2}</math> and <math>\frac{\omega_2}{2}</math> of the elliptic function, where the elliptic function is defined in such a way that

:<math>\Im(\tau) > 0</math>
is in the [[upper half-plane]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Half-Period Ratio |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/ |access-date=2024-02-03 |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |language=en}}</ref>

Quite often in the literature, &omega;<sub>1</sub> and &omega;<sub>2</sub> are defined to be the '''periods''' of an elliptic function rather than its half-periods. Regardless of the choice of notation, the ratio ω<sub>2</sub>/ω<sub>1</sub> of periods is identical to the ratio (ω<sub>2</sub>/2)/(ω<sub>1</sub>/2) of half-periods. Hence, the '''period ratio''' is the same as the "half-period ratio".

Note that the half-period ratio can be thought of as a simple number, namely, one of the parameters of elliptic functions, or it can be thought of as a function itself, because the half periods can be given in terms of the [[elliptic modulus]] or in terms of the [[nome (mathematics)|nome]].
See the pages on [[quarter period]] and [[elliptic integrals]] for additional definitions and relations on the arguments and parameters to elliptic functions.
